name: emu-channel-delivery
description: Three provisioned firmware pagers on one ether. The sender (0,0) broadcasts a channel message; both receivers must render it on their e-paper. Asserted by run_scenarios.sh via `screen-assert -min-nodes 2 -text 'HELLO BRAMBLE'`. All three share EMU_NETWORK_KEY so the mesh carries the frame. A receiver only auto-opens its Messages screen (where the text renders) for a message arriving after its own 10s message-idle threshold, measured from ITS boot; boots are staggered and a CPU-starved CI pod can lag a receiver's boot tens of seconds behind the sender's, so the send burst is long (12 sends, 8s apart, sender t=12s..100s) to guarantee sends land after every receiver's threshold no matter the lag. run_scenarios.sh waits event-driven and stops the run the moment both receivers have painted, so the long tail costs nothing on a fast box.
